FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by 
the Paper and its Products Sectional Committee, had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 


This Indian Standard was first published in1989. Map litho printing paper was originally a part of IS 1848 “Writing 
and printing paper’. Because of the request from Survey of India, a separate standard on map printing paper has 
been formulated as all the parameters required for map printing paper are not covered in IS 1848. 


The Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard decided to revise it further. During this revision, 
requirement of cobb, wax pick and brightness have been modified. Amendments issued so far have been 
amalgamated. Referred test methods have been updated. 


A scheme for labelling environment friendly products known as ECO Mark has been introduced at the instance of 
the Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change (MEF & CC), Government of India. The ECO Mark 
would be administered by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) under the BIS Act, 2016 as per the Resolutions 
No. 71 dated 21 February 1991 and No. 425 dated 28 October 1992 published in the Gazette of the Government 
of India. For a product to be eligible for marking with ECO logo, it shall also carry the BIS standard mark besides 
meeting additional optional environment friendly requirements. For this purpose, the Standard Mark of BIS would 
be a single mark being a combination of the BIS standard mark and the ECO logo. Requirements to be satisfied 
fora product to qualify for the BIS Standard Mark for ECO friendliness will be optional; manufacturing units will 
be free to opt for the ISI mark alone also. 


The composition of technical committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex A. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 “Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


Indian Standard 
MAP PRINTING PAPER — SPECIFICATION 


(First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes requirements, methods 
of sampling and tests for the map printing paper, 
commonly used for printing of maps to be kept for 
permanent records up to 50 years. 


2 REFERENCES

of this Indian Standard. At the time of publication, the 
editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject 
to revisions, and parties to agreements based on this 
Indian Standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of the 
Indian Standards.

3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the definitions of terms 
given in IS 4661 shall apply. 


4 REQUIREMENTS 


4.1 Furnish 


When tested according to IS 5285, the paper contain 
fully bleached pulps and will preferably varying 
percentage of cotton, hemp or soft wood fibres or a 
mixture of these. It shall be free from unbleached pulps 
or mechanical pulp. 


4.2 General 


Map printing papers shall be of uniform formation 
evenly finished and generally free from specks, holes 
and other blemishes. 


4.2.1 The paper shall be surface sized and with 
calendered finish. 


4.2.2 There shall be no curling defects during storage 
or during printing. 


4.2.3 There shall be absolutely no creasing defects 
during printing. 


4.2.4 The paper shall be free from fluff. 


4.3 Grammage 


The grammage shall not be less than 90 g/m?. However, 
when tested as prescribed in IS 1060 (Part 5/Sec 5) no 
single test result shall vary by more than + 5 percent 
from the nominal substance. Further the mean of 10 test 
results shall not vary from the nominal substance by 
more than + 2.5 percent. 


4.4 Sizes and Tolerance on Size 


The sizes shall be as prescribed by purchaser. The 
permissible deviation in length and width for untrimmed 
paper shall be + 0.5 percent. 


4.5 The pH value for map printing paper shall be 
not less than 6, when tested as prescribed in IS 1060 
(Part 4/Sec 7). 


4.6 In addition to the above requirements, the map 
printing papers shall also comply with the requirements 
given in Table 1. 


4.7 Accelerated Ageing 


The paper shall be subjected to accelerated ageing by 
heating in an oven maintained at 105 + 2 °C for 72 h, at 
the end of which the paper shall retain: 


a) at least 50 percent of its original folding endurance; 
and 


b) at least 75 percent of its original value of 
brightness. 


4.7.1 Dimensional Stability 


The paper shall be subjected to change in humidity 
from 20 percent to 75 percent and the change in 
dimensions shall not be more than 0.4 percent in MD 
and 0.8 percent in CD direction. 


4.8 Colour 


The paper shall be white or coloured as agreed to 
between the purchaser and the supplier. 


4.9 Additional Requirements for ECO Mark 
4.9.1 General Requirements 


4.9.1.1 The product shall conform to the requirements 
for quality and performance prescribed under clauses 
4.1 to 4.8. 


4.9.1.2 The manufacturer shall produce to BIS, the 
environmental consent clearance from the concerned 
State Pollution Control Board as per the provisions of 
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 
and Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 
1981 along with the authorisation, if required, under 
the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and the rules 
made thereunder, while applying for ECO Mark.

4.9.2 Product Specific Requirements 


a) The paper and paper boards manufactured out of 
pulp containing not less than 60 percent by weight 
of pulp made from materials other than bamboo, 
hardwoods, softwoods and reed. 


b) Recycled paper and paper board must be made 
from 100 percent waste paper. 


5 PACKING AND MARKING 


5.1 The packing of paper shall be done so as to ensure 
that the paper shall not get damaged due to handling 
and transportation and shall be as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier (see IS 6211). 


5.1.1 For ECO Mark, the product shall be packed in 
such packages which shall be recyclable/reusable or 
biodegradable. 


5.2 Each package shall be marked with the following 
particulars: 


a) Description and substance, in g/m? of the paper; 
b) Size of the paper; 
c) Lot number; 
d) Month and year of manufacture; and 
e) Name of manufacturer. 
5.2.1 For ECO Mark, following additional information 
may also be marked on the container/package: 


The criteria for which the product has been labelled 
with ECO Mark. 


5.2.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed there under, and the products 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


6 SAMPLING 
CONFORMITY 


AND CRITERIA OF 


6.1 Representative samples for test shall be drawn in 
accordance with 3 of IS 1060 (Part 1) : 1966. 


6.2 Tests 


From each of the packets selected from the lot (see 6.1), 
one sheet shall be taken out at random, These sheets 
shall constitute the sample. The sheets selected shall 
first be tested for general requirements given in 4.2. 
One test piece shall be cut from each sheet selected 
for each of the requirements from 4.3 to 4.5 and the 
characteristics mentioned in Table 1 and tested. A sheet 
not meeting the requirements for any one or more 
characteristics shall be considered as defective. 


6.3 Criterion for Conformity 


A lot shall be declared as conforming to all the 
requirements of this specification if the number of 
defective sheets found does not exceed the acceptance 
number. This acceptance number shall depend upon the 
size of the sample and shall be zero if the size is less 
than 13 and one if it is greater than or equal to 13. 


IS 12765 : 2021

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part ofthese publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
“BIS Catalogue” and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: CHD 15 (13772).
